claims.text: By default tofu plan refreshes before planning: it reads the state, and for each resource in it has the provider read the real object's current attributes, then compares those refreshed values with the configuration.
claims.source_hint: opentofu.org docs: CLI > tofu plan (refresh, -refresh=false); CLI > tofu refresh

claims.text: The hashicorp/kubernetes provider reports a label added by hand to a kubernetes_namespace_v1 whose labels attribute is set as an in-place update that removes it ('-> null'); in the captured run the plan header is 'will be updated in-place' and 'Plan: 0 to add, 1 to change, 0 to destroy.'
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang outputs/stage-3/scripts/devops/tofu-drift.txt (real run); search.opentofu.org hashicorp/kubernetes 3.3 kubernetes_namespace_v1 metadata.labels

claims.text: tofu plan -refresh-only shows the differences between the prior state and the refreshed objects, listed as '<address> has changed', and proposes no action on real objects.
claims.source_hint: opentofu.org docs: CLI > tofu plan > Planning modes (Refresh-only mode); tofu-drift.txt

claims.text: tofu apply -refresh-only updates the state to match the refreshed real objects and changes no real infrastructure object; afterwards a refresh-only plan shows no changes, while a normal plan still proposes changes where the files differ.
claims.source_hint: opentofu.org docs: CLI > tofu plan > Planning modes (Refresh-only); CLI > tofu refresh (deprecated alias of apply -refresh-only)

claims.text: OpenTofu reads and changes infrastructure only while you run a command such as plan or apply (the write–plan–apply loop is driven by commands).
claims.source_hint: opentofu.org/docs/intro/core-workflow/ (core workflow is a loop of commands; apply shows a plan before changing infrastructure)

claims.text: A Kubernetes control loop keeps comparing desired and current state and acts on the difference; a Deployment's ReplicaSet replaces a deleted Pod.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io docs: Concepts > Architecture > Controllers; Workloads > ReplicaSet

claims.text: An exit code is the number a command returns to the shell when it ends. tofu plan -detailed-exitcode returns 0 with no changes, 1 on error, 2 with changes; the captured run prints exit code 2 with the label, 0 after the apply.
claims.source_hint: opentofu.org docs: CLI > tofu plan > Other options (-detailed-exitcode); tofu-drift.txt

claims.text: A plain tofu apply (without -target or -refresh-only) plans the whole configuration, so it removes the hand-made label even when made for an unrelated change.
claims.source_hint: opentofu.org docs: CLI > tofu apply (creates a plan of all changes, then executes it)

claims.text: staging/platform/main.tf lines 26-37: module "platform" sources ../../../modules/donhang-platform with the sealing certificate/key files and pod_security_enforce = "baseline"; the module creates kubernetes_namespace_v1.donhang and kubernetes_secret_v1.sealing_key.

In the donhang-platform module, the namespace's labels are local.pod_security_labels: three keys pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce (var.pod_security_enforce), warn and audit (restricted); no owner label.

tofu-drift.sh: tofu_platform runs scripts/devops/tofu-env.sh staging platform; it labels namespace donhang owner=by-hand, plans with -detailed-exitcode (status kept via || status=$?), plans -refresh-only, then apply -auto-approve and a final -detailed-exitcode plan.
With set -e (set -euo pipefail), a command that exits non-zero stops the script unless it is part of a || list, as in 'cmd || status=$?'.
claims.source_hint: GNU Bash manual: The Set Builtin (-e exceptions for && and || lists)

claims.text: Annotations are a key-value map under metadata, like labels. In the captured run the refresh-only plan also lists kubernetes_secret_v1.sealing_key has changed, with only '+ annotations = {}' (not in state); the script never changes that Secret.

tofu apply -auto-approve applies without asking for 'yes'; in the captured run it prints 'Apply complete! Resources: 0 added, 1 changed, 0 destroyed.' and the namespace's labels no longer include owner.
claims.source_hint: opentofu.org docs: CLI > tofu apply (-auto-approve); tofu-drift.txt

claims.text: Adding the owner label to the namespace's labels in the files makes the refreshed object and configuration agree, so tofu plan -detailed-exitcode exits 0 and the label stays; production's platform layer calls the same donhang-platform module.
claims.source_hint: opentofu.org docs: CLI > tofu plan; examples/don-hang deploy/tofu/envs/production/platform/main.tf line 30 at stage-3

claims.text: When a hand-made change is right, prefer writing it into the configuration over applying the unchanged files or recording it with apply -refresh-only; opposing view: when the change was a mistake or a temporary debug aid, letting the next apply undo it is the fix.
claims.source_hint: opentofu.org docs: CLI > tofu plan > Planning modes (refresh-only: 'update configuration to match')

claims.text: kubectl label <type> <name> key=value adds a label to an existing object and prints '<type>/<name> labeled'.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io docs: kubectl reference > kubectl label; tofu-drift.txt
